strategy.summary: Identify old order blocks formed on the left side of a Market Maker Model. Once price transitions to the right side of the curve, trade the return to these 'reclaimed' order blocks, but strictly only when they overlap with other newly formed PD arrays.

timeframes.notes: He demonstrates looking at a 4-hour HTF for context and dropping to a 15-minute LTF to identify the Market Maker Model and overlapping arrays.

other: Requires an active Market Maker Model (a sell curve followed by a buy curve, or vice versa).

glossary.Reclaimed order block: An order block that formed on the first curve of a market maker model, got traded through, and now acts as support/resistance on the second curve.
glossary.Market maker buy model: A market profile consisting of a sell curve (price moving down to a HTF discount array) followed by a buy curve (price moving up).
glossary.Market maker sell model: A market profile consisting of a buy curve (price moving up to a HTF premium array) followed by a sell curve (price moving down).

custom_signals.name: market_maker_curve_shift
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price reaches a HTF discount/premium array, exhibits displacement with a market structure shift, and begins the second curve of a market maker model.

custom_signals.name: reclaimed_trade_through
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades back above/below an old order block from the first curve, making it 'reclaimed'.

custom_signals.name: overlapping_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: The reclaimed order block shares the exact same price zone as another PD array (FVG, mitigation block, breaker block, or standard order block).

sequence: Identify the two curves of a Market Maker Model (e.g., a sell curve reaching a HTF discount array, shifting into a buy curve).
Identify order blocks that formed on the left side of the curve (e.g., bullish order blocks forming during the downward sell curve as institutions accumulate).
Wait for price to shift into the right side of the curve and trade decisively past the old left-curve order block, officially making it a 'reclaimed order block'.
Filter out naked reclaimed order blocks. Only validate the reclaimed order block if it explicitly overlaps with another newly formed PD array (like an FVG, breaker, or mitigation block).
Enter on the return to this overlapping, high-confluence zone.

filters.text: Never trade a reclaimed order block in isolation. It MUST overlap with another PD array to avoid chart clutter and low-probability random bounces.

entry_rule.text: Enter when price retraces into the reclaimed order block that overlaps with another PD array.

strategy.notes: The primary lesson of this video is confluence as a filter for chart clutter. Reclaimed OBs are extremely common because they form throughout the entire left curve of a market maker model. The strategy relies completely on throwing out 90% of them and keeping only the ones stacked with FVGs or breakers.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price moves down forming a sell curve towards a HTF discount array. During this leg, institutions buy and form regular bullish order blocks.
Price hits the discount array, shifts market structure, and begins the upward buy curve.
Price trades above the old bullish order blocks from the sell curve, officially turning them into reclaimed order blocks that now act as support.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter explains the fundamental logic of a market maker model: institutions accumulate long positions during the sell curve, forming order blocks. Once the trend shifts to the buy curve, these same blocks become reclaimed and provide support.
